text:
maya (support): Opening thread. Customer reported sudden p95/p99 tail spikes after yesterday's quant profile promotion. They saw p95 go from ~120ms -> ~360ms and p99 up to ~1.1s on /v1/generate. They replayed traffic and attached logs. Request sample id: sample-9b3.

maya (support): model: rwl-large-1.2; quant_profile: int8-adaptive-v4 (promoted 2026-03-09); use_fp8=true in profile. workload: mostly long-context chat, median prompt ~900 tokens, occasional 2048. Traffic: sustained 150rps during repro.

derek (eng-runtime): thanks. any changes to batching, route config, or autoscale?

maya (support): no customer-side changes. Server-side we deployed profile globally on hosted pool at 02:15 UTC. Autoscale unchanged.

perf-bot: auto-detect: correlation between quant_profile rollout and tail latency increase for hosts in region us-west2. Kernel path switches logged around same timestamps.

sophia (eng-ml): sharing quick hypothesis: some layers are selecting fp8 microkernels which are great for throughput but on our Nvidia T4/RTX mix they sometimes introduce extra packing/unpacking steps and temporary buffers; with long KV cache writes those memcpy costs amplify p99. Also possible calibration mismatch for long seqs.

maya (support): pasted customer snippet from replay run:
```
[2026-03-10T05:33:11.201Z] INFO req=sample-9b3 kernel_select layer=18 -> fp8_opt
[2026-03-10T05:33:11.208Z] WARN req=sample-9b3 kv_cache_miss seq=0->128
[2026-03-10T05:33:12.412Z] WARN req=sample-9b3 memcpy size=28MB duration_ms=132.7
[2026-03-10T05:33:12.762Z] ERROR req=sample-9b3 token_emit duration_ms=1104.6
```

derek (eng-runtime): can you attach the per-op trace (times) and the kernel selection table for that request? also confirm whether this is on shared hosted pool.

maya (support): attached inline trace:
```
trace sample-9b3:
  layer=18 op=attn_compute kernel=fp8_opt time_ms=54.9
  op=kv_store memcpy size=28MB time_ms=132.7
  op=token_emit time_ms=1104.6
```

perf-bot: analysis: elevated memcpy + fp8_opt op latency correlate with token_emit tail. Candidate root: fp8 path plus KV cache warm causing large memcopies and GC stalls.

omar (sre): operational impact: multiple customers on hosted pool near us-west2 saw elevated p99 during window. Recommend immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact.

sophia (eng-ml): immediate mitigations we can try: (1) disable fp8 selection in int8-adaptive-v4 (set use_fp8=false) for affected hosts; (2) enable runtime fallback: if per-token latency > 300ms for N tokens, force fp16 kernels for remainder; (3) re-run calibration with long-context dataset and increase warmup/correction for layers showing fp8 instability.

derek (eng-runtime): control API snippet to apply model variant override to disable fp8 on the pool (can narrow by host tag):
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/v1/models/rwl-large-1.2/variants/quant/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"quant_profile":"int8-adaptive-v4","overrides":{"use_fp8":"false"},"target_hosts":"pool:hosted-us-west2"}'
```

maya (support): I pushed a 10% canary override for the customer's traffic 12 minutes ago. Early numbers from their replay: p95 dropped from 360ms -> 160ms, p99 dropped to ~420ms. Still above original baseline but much better.

omar (sre): good. let's make an alert: if p99(/v1/generate) > 600ms for 5m we auto-roll back to previous profile (int8-adaptive-v3) for that host pool. I'll add the monitor now.

derek (eng-runtime): added a short rollback playbook to the ops runbook:
1) apply override disable fp8 for affected pool
2) monitor p95/p99 for 15m
3) if stable, expand canary 10->25->50->100 in 20m increments
4) if not stable, rollback to previous profile id int8-adaptive-v3

sophia (eng-ml): I'll start calibration job with these params and include customer prompts in the corpus:
```
calibration_job:
  profile_base: int8-adaptive-v4
  dataset: long_context_mixed_clients_v1 + customer_sample_9b3
  warmup_steps: 96
  per_layer_thresholds: increase
  prefer_fp16_on_tail: true
```

maya (support): customer notes: they can accept a temporary rollback and want notification when full rollout is safe. They also supplied an internal small corpus that helped reproduce.

derek (eng-runtime): timeline & owners: @sophia will produce new profile candidate by EOD, run internal canary; @omar will create and enforce monitor + auto-rollback rule; I'll handle canary expansion and validate kernel-level telemetry.

perf-bot: scheduled a retrospective perf job comparing int8-adaptive-v3 vs v4 across seq lengths [128,512,1024,2048] on hardware mix (T4, A10G).

omar (sre): additional infra tweak: increase kv cache prewarm entries for hosts serving long-seq customers to reduce memcpy on first requests; set prewarm_count=128 for tagged hosts. I'll coordinate with infra.

maya (support): after expanding the canary to 25% (30m), p95 stable at ~150ms, p99 ~360ms. Customer accepted controlled rollforward if we continue monitoring.

sophia (eng-ml): note for engineering: add lightweight runtime heuristic so kernel selector considers memcpy overhead (estimated temp buffer size) before choosing fp8_opt. Also add metric: kernel_switch_count per-request to catch frequent toggles.

derek (eng-runtime): agreed. action items being added to sprint: runtime heuristic, calibration re-run, alert + auto-rollback, kv cache prewarm change. Will open tickets.

maya (support): closing loop with customer now. will keep thread open for final rollforward confirmation. thanks all :white_check_mark:
